discourse.excerpt: It is naive to think that one alone is the doer of one's actions. All the things in the world are not intended for the exclusive enjoyment of any single person. They are to be shared by all.
discourse.theme: True service knows no distinctions — nothing in this world is for one person's exclusive enjoyment; all is to be shared.
discourse.title: Service without distinctions

reflection: Swami cuts through the 'mine and thine' habit: nothing in this world is meant for one person's exclusive enjoyment — all of it is to be shared by all. When you act without clinging to the fruits, the action itself becomes yoga, Divine communion. Today, share one thing freely — a meal, a skill, your time — with no thought of return. That is service without distinctions. (Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 17, 18 Nov 1984)
seva_nudge: Offer a ride to the next Sunday bhajan at Sai Prema Nilayam Riverside to someone who otherwise could not come — arrange it quietly, no fanfare.
